AWS Well-Architected Framework
Last updated:
November 16, 2026
(
Release notes
)
The AWS Well-Architected Framework helps you understand the pros and cons of decisions
    you make while building systems on AWS. Using the Framework helps you learn architectural best
    practices for designing and operating secure, reliable, efficient, cost-effective, and
    sustainable workloads in the AWS Cloud. It provides a way for you to consistently measure your
    architectures against best practices and identify areas for improvement. The process for
    reviewing an architecture is a constructive conversation about architectural decisions, and is
    not an audit mechanism. We believe that having well-architected systems greatly increases the
    likelihood of business success.
AWS Solutions Architects have years of experience architecting solutions across a wide
    variety of business verticals and use cases. We have helped design and review thousands of
    customers' architectures on AWS. From this experience, we have identified best practices and
    core strategies for architecting systems in the cloud.
The AWS Well-Architected Framework documents a set of foundational questions that help
    you to understand if a specific architecture aligns well with cloud best practices. The
    framework provides a consistent approach to evaluating systems against the qualities you expect
    from modern cloud-based systems, and the remediation that would be required to achieve those
    qualities. As AWS continues to evolve, and we continue to learn more from working with our
    customers, we will continue to refine the definition of well-architected.
This framework is intended for those in technology roles, such as chief technology officers
    (CTOs), architects, developers, and operations team members. It describes AWS best practices
    and strategies to use when designing and operating a cloud workload, and provides links to
    further implementation details and architectural patterns. For more information, see the
AWS
      Well-Architected homepage
.
AWS also provides services for reviewing your workloads. For more detail, see
What is
      AWS Well-Architected?
Architecture
From centralized to distributed
In traditional environments, organizations often have a centralized architecture team
        that acts as an overlay to product or feature teams. These teams verify that other teams
        follow best practices and maintain standards across the organization.
In cloud environments, this model does not scale. The pace of change, the breadth of
        available services, and the need for teams to move independently require a different
        approach. Instead of centralizing architecture decisions, distribute architectural
        capability to the teams that build and operate workloads.
This shift requires two things to work:
Practices
that enable each team to make sound architectural
            decisions. Practices include shared standards, design patterns, reference architectures,
            and access to subject matter experts who can review designs and raise the bar.
Mechanisms
that verify standards are being met without requiring
            manual oversight. Mechanisms include automated compliance checks, architecture fitness
            functions, and infrastructure-as-code policies that enforce guardrails.
When you distribute architectural ownership, every team is responsible for creating
        architectures that follow best practices. To help teams gain and maintain this capability,
        provide access to experts who can review designs and share knowledge across the
        organization.
Architecture governance at scale
Effective governance in a distributed model relies on automation rather than manual
        review. Consider the following approaches:
Use infrastructure as code to define and enforce architectural patterns.
            Infrastructure definitions become reviewable, testable, and versionable like application
            code.
Implement automated guardrails through service control policies, permission
            boundaries, and configuration rules that prevent non-compliant deployments rather than
            detecting them after the fact.
Record architectural decisions using a lightweight, consistent format (such as
            architecture decision records) so that teams can understand the context behind past
            choices. This preserves institutional knowledge and reduces repeated debates.
Conduct Well-Architected reviews at key milestones in the workload lifecycle. These
            reviews are constructive conversations about architectural decisions, not audits. Use
            them to identify risks, share knowledge across teams, and track improvements over time.
Evolutionary architecture
Cloud architectures are not static. They evolve as business requirements change, new
        services become available, and teams learn from operating their workloads. Design for change
        rather than designing for a fixed end state.
An evolutionary approach to architecture means:
Making decisions reversible where possible. Prefer approaches that allow you to
            change direction without significant rework.
Using data to inform architectural decisions. Collect metrics on how your workload
            performs and use that data to validate or challenge your assumptions.
Testing architectural changes through experimentation. Use canary deployments,
            feature flags, and A/B testing to validate changes incrementally before full commitment.
Treating your architecture as a living artifact. Update documentation, diagrams,
            and decision records as the architecture evolves. Mark milestones at key changes to
            track how the architecture has developed over time.
The role of the Well-Architected Framework
The AWS Well-Architected Framework provides a consistent approach for evaluating
        architectures against the qualities you expect from cloud-based systems. It codifies best
        practices that have emerged from designing, building, and reviewing thousands of workloads
        on AWS.
Use the Framework to:
Establish a common language for discussing architectural decisions across teams.
Identify risks in your technology portfolio by reviewing workloads against best
            practices.
Find themes across teams that can be addressed through shared mechanisms, training,
            or organizational changes.
Track improvements over time by conducting reviews at milestones and comparing
            results across review cycles.
Technology leaders carrying out Well-Architected reviews across workloads gain
        visibility into the risks in their technology portfolio and can identify where investment in
        shared capabilities will have the greatest impact.
Lens availability
Custom lenses extend the best practice guidance provided by AWS Well-Architected Tool. AWS WA Tool allows you
      to create your own
custom lenses
, or to use
      lenses created by others that have been shared with you.
There are two custom lenses provided for the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
Note
The Cloud Foundations custom lens contains the best practices in the
Foundations
section.
The Cloud Workloads custom lens contains the updated Well-Architected Framework pillars.
Well-Architected Cloud Foundations
Well-Architected Cloud Workloads
To begin reviewing your workloads, download and import either custom lens into AWS Well-Architected Tool
      from the public
AWS
        Well-Architected custom lens GitHub repository
.
